transcript.text: Hi everyone. We're approaching the readiness review for the real-time collaboration service launch on Monday at 09:00 UTC. The draft plan has us starting at 10% of accounts, up to 10,000 concurrent connections, default 5-second retry interval, primary production region storage, and 90-day transcript retention. Before I finalize and record the binding policy, I need each of you — backend engineering, reliability, privacy, and customer success — to do your final check-in. Let's go around and hear any concerns or sign-offs.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a concern before we finalize. While investigating an unrelated mobile performance report this afternoon, I confirmed that mobile clients resume from background in bursts and currently retry every 5 seconds, which can create a reconnect storm. The rollout policy should set the retry interval to exactly 30 seconds. I have not yet filed the client-library ticket.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical capacity concern. About 20 minutes ago, I completed a production-traffic replay and confirmed that the collaboration cluster's safe connection ceiling for Monday is exactly 6,000 concurrent connections — not the 10,000 in the draft plan. The autoscaling limit hasn't been updated yet because the replay results are still being attached to the capacity worksheet. We need to lower the concurrent connection cap to 6,000 before this plan is finalized.

transcript.text: I need to flag two privacy compliance issues with the draft plan. I finished a privacy review this morning and confirmed that collaboration content for EU accounts must remain in the EU processing region — the draft plan's use of the primary production region would violate that requirement. Additionally, session transcripts must be deleted after exactly 30 days, not the 90 days in the draft plan. I have not yet opened the compliance ticket because legal was still reviewing the wording.
